plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $31.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no benefit to bidding above or below my true value of $6. Bidding exactly $6 ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than what I'd pay, and I never overpay since the price is determined by the second-highest bid, not mine.

My value is $0, meaning any positive payment would result in a loss. Since this is a second-price auction, bidding my true value ($0) is optimal: if I win, I'd pay something ≥0 which could still cost me money if I bid higher than 0. Bidding exactly $0 ensures I never pay more than my value, avoiding any possible loss while still allowing a win if others also bid $0 (resulting in $0 profit).
